issues.description: The template's Lecture.addGuestStudents method has a different parameter list than specified in the problem statement and implemented in the solution. The problem UML and instructions require addGuestStudents(int) (single int parameter), and the solution implements public void addGuestStudents(int). However, the template declares public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents, boolean validateInput) which adds an extra boolean parameter. This mismatch can confuse students about the required signature and cause test/compile issues if they follow the exercise description or the solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the template with the problem specification and solution by changing the template method signature to public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents) (remove the boolean parameter). If validation behavior is desired, either implement it internally without changing the signature or add an overloaded helper method, and update the problem statement to explicitly mention the extra parameter if that was intended.

issues.description: The problem statement and the solution define a method addGuestStudents(int) that accepts a single integer parameter, but the template repository declares addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents, boolean validateInput) with an extra boolean parameter. This mismatched method signature creates a naming/API inconsistency that will confuse students mapping the exercise requirements to the provided starter code and the expected solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the template method signature with the problem statement and solution by changing the template declaration to: public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents) { ... } . If the boolean validateInput parameter is intentional, update the problem statement and solution to document and use the two-parameter signature consistently.
